full_judgment:
1. In this Rule Nisi, issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the impugned order under Nathi No. S/68/CEVT (Appeal)/Khulna/M/s. Madina Agency/2020-21/144 dated 22-3-2021 issued by the respondent No. 7 on behalf of the respondent No. 6 rejecting the appeal filed by the petitioner, purportedly under section 194(1) of the Customs Act, 1969 when evidently said appeal has been preferred by the petitioner under Rule 22 of the Customs Agents Licensing Rules, 2016 challenging the order dated 3-12-2020 passed by the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 canceling the C&F License No. 20/LC-CA/1990 dated 11-6-1990 of the petitioner and imposing penalty of Taka 2,00,000 (as contained in Annexure-H to the supplementary affidavit), should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. However, at the time of issuance of the Rule, the operation of the impugned order dated 22-3-2021 passed under Nathi No. S/68/CEVT (Appeal)/Khulna/M/s. Madina Agency/2020-21/144 dated 22-3-2021 by the respondent No. 6 (Annexure-H to the supplementary-affidavit) has been stayed by this Court for a prescribed period. 

 34. The impugned order under Nathi No. S/68/CEVT(Appeal)/Khulna/M/s. Madina Agency/2020-21/144 dated 22-3-2021 passed by the respondent No. 7 on behalf of the respondent No. 6 rejecting the appeal filed by the petitioner, purportedly under section 194(1) of the Customs Act, 1969 (Annexure-H to the supplementary-affidavit), is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect.
